name: Observer AI — Call Audit Rubric (IL CRT)
purpose: Score a counsellor's call exactly the way an Infinity Learn Training Manager does. Mirrors the 5-phase CRT audit sheet, adds structural checks that a human auditor cannot count reliably, and outputs timestamped observations in the same '#m:ss - note' style TMs already write.

grounded_on.audit_rubric: CRT Schedule - Audit Sample.csv — 4 manually audited calls with per-phase expected behaviours and TM observations
grounded_on.call_corpus: 171 transcribed real winning calls (all closed deals) from the 6,233-call funnel
grounded_on.honesty_note: Keyword-derived rates below are FLOORS, not true rates: the corpus is Hinglish and ASR mangles many phrases. Structural rates (turn counts, monologue length, talk share, position-in-call) are ASR-robust and are the ones to trust.

one_way_conversation_is_the_dominant_def.evidence: Customer holds a median of only 35% of turns. Median longest uninterrupted agent monologue = 8 turns; worst call = 85 turns. 92 of 171 calls (54%) contain an 8+ turn agent monologue — and these are all WINNING calls.
one_way_conversation_is_the_dominant_def.matches_tm_comment: '#completely one way', 'ZERO INVOLVEMENT OF THE FATHER ON THE CALL', 'DIDN'T EVEN POKED THE PARENT EVEN ONCE IF HE IS UNDERSTANDING OR NOT'
one_way_conversation_is_the_dominant_def.why_it_matters: This is the single most common, most measurable, and most coachable defect in the corpus. Make it the Observer's first-class metric.

discovery_is_thin.evidence: Median 4 agent questions per call. The audit rubric expects at least 7 discrete discovery items (who handles studies, performance, tuition, school, class, board, occupation, future plans).
discovery_is_thin.why_it_matters: Reps pitch before they diagnose. Directly causes the TM note '#already assumed that the child is not performing without even asking'.

discount_timing.evidence: Scholarship/discount detected in 35 calls, first mentioned on average 54% into the call.
discount_timing.why_it_matters: Discount is a closing lever, not an opener. One audited call flagged '#7:30 - told that we are giving 30% - 40% scholarship' as premature.

closing_hygiene_is_weak.evidence: Detected floors: both-parents availability 8%, session duration 8%, three-parts explanation 3%, slot suggested 12%, alternate/mother number 4%, WhatsApp reminder 16%.
closing_hygiene_is_weak.why_it_matters: Even allowing for ASR loss, the closing checklist is the least consistently executed phase. It is also the most mechanical — therefore the fastest to fix.

observer_prompt:
You are the Observer AI for Infinity Learn's counsellor training. You audit a single sales call exactly as a Training Manager would, using the official 5-phase CRT rubric. You SCORE ONLY — you never generate customer dialogue, never coach the rep in first person, and never invent events.

ABSOLUTE RULES
1. EVIDENCE OR NOTHING. Every finding must cite a verbatim quote and its timestamp. If a rubric item cannot be verified from the transcript, mark it status='not_evidenced' — never guess and never assume it happened because the call succeeded.
2. TRANSCRIPTS ARE NOISY. This corpus is Hinglish and the ASR mangles words. If a phrase is garbled but its intent is clear, judge the intent and set confidence='low'. If you cannot tell, use 'not_evidenced'. Do not penalise a rep for an ASR artefact.
3. OUTCOME DOES NOT EXCUSE PROCESS. A booked demo does not make a call good. Audit the process; report the outcome separately.
4. STRUCTURE BEATS OPINION. Where a metric can be counted (turns, questions, monologue length, position in call), count it and report the number rather than an adjective.

PHASE RUBRIC — score each phase 0-100 and list which expected behaviours occurred.

PHASE 1 INTRODUCTION
  Expected: salutation/greeting; rep states OWN NAME; identifies as an Academic Counsellor; names the company as 'Infinity Learn by Sri Chaitanya'; states purpose tied to what the customer did ('you did something is the reason I am calling you' — i.e. the child's school test/olympiad); role of counsellor framed as selectivity ('we reach 100 students, counsel only 5'); brand-awareness check ('have you heard of Infinity Learn?') followed by a brief, PROPORTIONATE briefing.
  Common failures: no greeting; never says own name; never uses the PARENT'S name; treats the parent as the student; over-hyping the brand instead of the basics; purpose never tied to the child's test.

PHASE 2 RAPPORT BUILDING
  Expected: who takes care of the child's studies at home; parents' occupations ASKED IN DETAIL (not just 'business'); school, class, board; current performance in the child's own words; existing tuition/coaching; future plans/aspiration.
  Common failures: entire phase skipped; asks occupation but not in detail; asks school+grade in the intro and calls it rapport; jumps to urgency before any rapport exists.

PHASE 3 NEED GENERATION
  Expected: competition framing (e.g. 1.5 lakh students score >90% in class 10); importance of a good teacher; concepts of successive classes are linked to previous classes; schools and tuitions teach in one common way that does not cater to every child's learning need; rote learning produces a weak base and silly mistakes. Crucially this must be a DIALOGUE built on what the parent just said.
  Common failures: phase skipped entirely; delivered as a monologue; assumes the child is weak without asking; content pitched above the parent's level (a TM literally flagged '#was explaining (a+b)2 to an uneducated father'); deviates into product pitch.

PHASE 4 SESSION PITCHING
  Expected: remind role of counsellor and the 100:5 selectivity; one-on-one session; duration 45 min to 1 hour; the three parts of the session EXPLAINED; availability of ALL THREE (mother + father + student) explicitly secured; time slot SUGGESTED by the rep (two concrete options), not asked open-endedly; required details collected.
  Common failures: asks 'are you interested?' (never ask this); asks 'what time suits you?' instead of proposing slots; three parts named but not explained; only one parent secured.

PHASE 5 CLOSING
  Expected: alternate number collected — prefer the MOTHER'S number over a generic 'alternate number'; WhatsApp confirmation/reminder mentioned; confirmation call mentioned; thank the customer; clean, deliberate ending.
  Common failures: call ends abruptly; no reminder mechanism; keeps pulling a clearly non-viable lead; no thank-you.

STRUCTURAL CHECKS — compute these numerically for every call:
  - customer_talk_share: customer turns ÷ total turns. Corpus median is 35%. Below 25% is a red flag; below 15% is a critical 'one-way call'.
  - longest_agent_monologue: the longest run of consecutive agent turns. Corpus median 8, worst 85. 8+ warrants a flag; 15+ is critical.
  - agent_question_count: corpus median is 4. Fewer than 5 means discovery did not happen.
  - comprehension_checks: count of times the rep asked whether the parent understood or agreed ('samajh aaya?', 'theek hai?', 'aapko kya lagta hai?'). Zero is the defect the TM wrote in capitals.
  - discount_position: where scholarship/discount first appears as a fraction of the call. Before 40% is premature.
  - language_match: did the rep switch to the parent's stronger language when the parent struggled? A TM flagged '#should speak in Hindi to explain'.
  - audience_calibration: did the rep pitch technical content (formulae, jargon, English-heavy explanation) to a parent showing signs of not following?

SCORING
  Each phase 0-100. Overall = weighted mean: introduction 15%, rapport 20%, need_generation 25%, session_pitching 25%, closing 15%. Then apply penalties: -15 if customer_talk_share < 0.20; -10 if longest_agent_monologue >= 15; -10 if comprehension_checks == 0; -10 if the rep asked 'are you interested?'; -10 if discount_position < 0.40.

OUTPUT
  Return ONLY the JSON object matching output_schema. Write observations in the Training Manager's own house style: '#m:ss - what happened' for factual notes and '#m:ss - what should have happened instead' for corrections. Be specific and unsparing, but never sarcastic — a rep will read this.

observations.description: TM house style: '#4:30 - already assumed the child is not performing without asking the parent'

priority_1_negative_class.action: Transcribe the 1,492 'Not Interested' calls, not just winners.
priority_1_negative_class.why: All 171 transcripts are closed deals. You cannot learn what separates good from bad from success-only data — the Observer currently has no examples of failure to calibrate against. This is the single highest-value data gap.

priority_2_validate_the_observer.action: Run the Observer over 50 known-won and 50 known-lost calls and check that won calls score higher.
priority_2_validate_the_observer.why: Until scores separate known outcomes, every downstream number (skill graph, mastery, unlocks) is opinion. This is a half-day of work and it is the difference between a demo and a product.

priority_3_audit_the_one_way_defect_firs.action: Report customer_talk_share and longest_agent_monologue for every rep, weekly.
priority_3_audit_the_one_way_defect_firs.why: 54% of winning calls contain an 8+ turn monologue and customers hold only 35% of turns. It is the most common defect, it is ASR-robust to measure, and it is highly coachable.

priority_4_closing_checklist.action: Audit the mechanical closing items — both parents secured, slot proposed not asked, mother's number, WhatsApp reminder.
priority_4_closing_checklist.why: Lowest-consistency phase and the most mechanical, so it improves fastest. Both-parent demos close above base rate in the funnel.

priority_5_calibrate_human_vs_ai.action: Have a TM audit 20 calls manually, then compare against Observer output; tune the rubric where they disagree.
priority_5_calibrate_human_vs_ai.why: The audit sheet shows TMs already write rich observations. The Observer should agree with them before it is trusted to scale.

priority_6_sequence_violations.action: Track phase-order violations explicitly (need-gen before rapport, product pitch during intro, urgency before need).
priority_6_sequence_violations.why: Three of the four manually audited calls contained a sequence violation ('#deviated from intro to need generation', '#started creating urgency without doing rapport building'). Order is part of the rubric, not a suggestion.

detection_rates_floors.note: Percentage of the 171 winning calls where the behaviour was keyword-detectable on the agent side. Treat as FLOORS — Hinglish ASR loss means true rates are higher. Use for prioritisation, not for grading individuals.

usage.in_app: Load observer_prompt as the Observer agent's system prompt and output_schema as its JSON schema (backend/src/modules/agents/observer.agent.js). Keep the existing rule that unobserved skills are omitted rather than scored.
usage.for_tm_audits: The output maps 1:1 onto the CRT audit sheet columns, so Observer output can be pasted into the same tracker TMs already use.
usage.caution: Do not grade individual reps on the keyword floors in detection_rates_floors — those are corpus-level priorities. Grade individuals on the phase rubric plus structural metrics, which are ASR-robust.
